clue.text: Open golf course that's open for lunch?

definitions.meaning: Royal St George's at ... in Kent is a links course that hosts the Open Championship
an open ... is a slice of bread with a topping and no lid, eaten at lunchtime

explanation.surface: A golf club hosting the big tournament also welcomes visitors to its restaurant at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'open' is lower-case and means a sandwich with no top slice; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town names both a championship links course and the familiar bread-based lunch item.

clue.text: Meet company initially making programme

parts.note: a court or committee sits, i.e. meets in session

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of the word making

explanation.surface: A broadcaster gathering its firm together to plan a new show.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a type of television programme.

clue.text: Northern crews dropping first of two Arab big noises?

indicators.note: dropping says a letter is shed from the crews word

parts.note: rowing eights are crews of eight oarsmen

indicators.note: first of says take the opening letter of the word two

explanation.surface: Boat crews from the north losing a member, with talk of Arabian notables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes the T (from 'first of two') from EIGHTS. 'Arab big noises' is cryptic: an Arab is a horse, and its loud noises are whinnies.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a breed of horse, and the sounds a horse makes loudly are its whinnies.

clue.text: Intense activity with new English part of competition

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of with are formed afresh in another order

parts.note: a heat is one preliminary round of a race or contest

explanation.surface: A frantic new English round of a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges WITH into WHIT, which takes E and then HEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a state of intense passion or furious activity, as of metal heated past red.

clue.text: Various arc lights on, flooding jail? No hope of exercising these privately!

definitions.text: No hope of exercising these privately!

indicators.note: flooding means the shuffled letters surround and engulf the word for jail
various suggests the letters of arc lights on in a different, assorted order

parts.note: jug is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Arc lights pour over a prison, so inmates have no chance of private intimacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges ARC LIGHTS ON, which 'flooding' wraps round JUG. The definition is cryptic: prisoners under floodlights cannot enjoy these privately.
explanation.definitionFit: Married couples' entitlement to sexual relations is something prisoners lack the opportunity to exercise in private.

clue.text: Channel Islands left back's parallel

indicators.note: back signals that the joined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A left-back footballer from Jersey or Guernsey is compared to another player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses CI + PORT, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude, i.e. parallels.

clue.text: Message received: "See him after jolly on brigantine, say"

definitions.meaning: radio operators say this word to confirm a message has been heard

definitions.text: See him after jolly on brigantine, say
definitions.meaning: the Jolly ... is a pirate flag, so this name follows jolly on a pirate ship

explanation.surface: A sailor confirms a message: he'll see a crewmate after some fun aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing ship, the kind a pirate might fly the skull and crossbones from.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio voice procedure this word means the message has been received and understood.

clue.text: Concert books top female backer

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at London's BBC Proms
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the top woman

explanation.surface: A concert reserves the leading lady as its financial supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous summer series of BBC concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A promoter supports and finances an event or cause, so is a backer of it.

clue.text: College needs no changes to contract

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of needs no are rearranged

explanation.surface: A college insists its agreement must not be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges NEEDS NO into ONDENSE, which follows C. 'contract' looks like a noun; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense something is to shrink or compress it, i.e. make it contract.

clue.text: Cosmetic display or display of cosmetics?

definitions.meaning: a superficial show put on to create a favourable impression
arranging goods, such as make-up, in a shop window for passers-by

explanation.walkthrough: The two halves swap 'cosmetic' between its figurative sense, merely superficial, and its literal one, make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both arranging a shop's window and putting a misleadingly attractive face on something.

clue.text: Instinct lacking in teacher's work

indicators.note: lacking says the following word is taken away from the instinct word

parts.note: intuition is instinctive knowing

explanation.surface: Someone without natural instinct is not suited to a teacher's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes IN from the start of INTUITION.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching or instruction is the work a tutor or teacher does.

clue.text: Like some nails? Ring now — put in order

indicators.note: put in order tells us to rearrange the letters of ring now properly

explanation.surface: A command to phone a salon now to book a manicure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in order' rearranges RING NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Toenails can grow into the flesh at their edges, a painful condition.

clue.text: Sandy's routine task moving round to the front

indicators.note: moving says the round letter is shifted from its place in the chore word
to the front says where that shifted letter ends up: at the very start

parts.note: a chore is a dull, routine task
O is a round letter

explanation.surface: Sandy's daily job involves going round to the front of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving ... to the front' takes the O of CHORE to the start. 'Sandy' looks like a name; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment, the colour of sand.

clue.text: Rare pair of foreign articles prof examined first

parts.note: un is French for a and der is German for the
a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: first says take the opening letter of the word examined

explanation.surface: An unusual pair of articles from abroad, which a professor examined before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' is used in its cooking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare meat is lightly cooked, i.e. not cooked through.

clue.text: They could be trained as trowel- makers maybe

definitions.text: They could be trained as trowel- makers maybe

indicators.note: being trained into a new form suggests the letters of trowel makers are rearranged

explanation.surface: Apprentices could learn to produce garden tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be trained as' rearranges TROWEL MAKERS; the whole clue also describes the answer, since trowels are made of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftspeople who shape metal could plausibly be taught to manufacture trowels.

clue.text: Check army's put more beef in

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a force is an army or body of troops

explanation.surface: An inspection finds the army has bulked up with extra meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' means strength, not meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen something is to add muscle or beef to it.

clue.text: A nation defends popular element

indicators.note: defends means the nation word surrounds and protects the popular word

parts.note: a state is a nation
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A country protects a well-liked part of itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defends' means the nation surrounds the popular word, rather than the usual sense of guarding something.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatine is a radioactive chemical element, number 85.

clue.text: Plucky players, rare characters abroad wearing headgear

indicators.note: wearing means the other pieces are covered by the headgear word

parts.note: hats are headgear
R is an abbreviation for rare, used for example in coin catalogues
pi is a Greek letter, so pis are characters from abroad

explanation.surface: Brave musicians, unusual figures from overseas, in hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucky' means they pluck strings, not that they are brave. R for rare is a coin-collectors' abbreviation; Greek letters are 'characters abroad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of the harp pluck its strings, making them plucky in a punning sense.

clue.text: Dope spread product from mill across island

parts.note: to scatter is to spread about

indicators.note: across means the mill product stretches over and around the island letter

parts.note: bran is a by-product of milling grain

explanation.surface: Drugs being spread around an island along with milled grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts I inside BRAN. 'Dope' looks like a drug; it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid or foolish person, much like a forgetful, disorganised one.

clue.text: Oscar's successor crosses first of many small plains

indicators.note: crosses means the successor word straddles the following letter

parts.note: in the NATO alphabet Oscar, for O, is followed by Papa, for P

indicators.note: first of says take the opening letter of the word many

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner's successor passes over many small plains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crosses' puts M inside PAPA, and S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast grassy plains of South America.

clue.text: Count is aware of being caught

indicators.note: being caught by the ear means this word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to sense something is to be aware of it

explanation.surface: A nobleman knows he is about to be arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being caught' means heard: SENSES sounds like the answer. 'Count' looks like a nobleman; it is a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official tally of a population.

clue.text: After a bath TV lord returns plant

parts.note: Bath is a spa town, and a spa is a place to bathe

indicators.note: returns indicates the lord's name is written backwards

parts.note: Lord Sugar is the businessman who presents the UK version of The Apprentice

explanation.surface: A television peer comes back after a soak in the tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses SUGAR to give RAGUS; Alan Sugar is a British businessman and peer known from TV's The Apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a plant grown for its edible shoots.

clue.text: Man of many words, I set up in arts centre

indicators.note: in places the reversed self word within the middle of arts
centre says take the middle letters of the word arts
set up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: A wordy man installs himself in an arts centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses EGO to OGE, placed 'in' RT, the centre of 'arts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous thesaurus, a book full of words.

clue.text: Foxtrot with limping lover

parts.note: Foxtrot is the NATO alphabet word for F
lame means limping

explanation.surface: Dancing a foxtrot with a partner who is hobbling.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former sweetheart, so the word means a lover.

clue.text: Understanding's close to being achieved

definitions.meaning: a goal that is ... is near

explanation.surface: Comprehension is almost reached.
explanation.definitionFit: As one word it means perception; as two words it means visible and nearly attained.

clue.text: Bursts in Irish game puts United off

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: off says the United letter is removed from puts

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: An Irish match sends Manchester United packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes U from PUTS to leave PTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to enter forcibly or suddenly, i.e. burst in.

clue.text: Inferior bunch of skiers at Zermatt

indicators.note: bunch of says a group of consecutive letters is taken from the phrase skiers at Zermatt

explanation.surface: A sneer at a poor group of skiers at the Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunch of' picks the run of letters across skiERS AT Zermatt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes a substitute product, usually inferior to the real thing.

clue.text: Frenchman recalled his local escape routes

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the name is written in reverse

parts.note: Serge is a French man's name
ses is the French for his, local in the sense of the language used there

explanation.surface: A Frenchman remembers the way out of his local bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses SERGE to EGRES. 'local' looks like a pub; here it means in the local language.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is a way out, so the plural means exits or escape routes.
